author: Gould, 1848
summary: 우리나라에서는 제주도, 강화도 등지에서 보인다. 번식지에서는 고원 호숫가의 자갈밭이나 흐르는 냇가에 살며, 땅 위를 가볍고 재빠르게 달리며 먹이를 찾고 칼새처럼 빠르고 힘차게 난다. 곤충을 즐겨 먹는다. 몽골과 바이칼 등지에서 번식하고 오스트레일리아에서 겨울을 난다.

art.subject: Oriental Plover (Charadrius veredus), adult male in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean islands on spring passage (March–May): crown and hindcrown pale brown; forehead, lores, cheeks, chin and throat white, rear ear-coverts pale brown, a pale buff supercilium, so the whole head looks pale and white-faced; back, wings and tail pale grey-brown, the tail tipped white; a broad rusty-chestnut band across the upper breast bordered below by a black band; belly, flanks and undertail pure white. Slender black bill; dark eye; long dull yellow legs.
art.pose: running lightly over open ground in search of insects
art.scene: Korean island in spring: short-grass field and gravel flats beside a stream under an open sky; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male breeding, side view standing upright on short grass: pale brown crown and upperparts, white face and throat with a buff supercilium, broad rusty-chestnut breast band edged black below, pure white belly and flanks, slender black bill, long dull yellow legs, wingtips projecting beyond the tail
adult male breeding, front view: white throat and face, rusty-chestnut upper-breast band with a black band beneath it, white belly, long yellowish legs
art.build: Slender, long-legged plover, about 22.5cm long, a little smaller than Pacific Golden Plover; small rounded head, slim neck and long body, standing tall. Bill slender, straight and fine, about as long as the head. Legs long, with much bare tibia. Very long wings: at rest the wingtips project clearly beyond the tail tip. In flight long, pointed, almost plain brown wings and dusky underwings; flies fast and dashing like a swift.
avoid: Do not paint a black mask or a black forehead bar — those mark Greater and Lesser Sand Plovers.
Do not paint a short-legged, dumpy plover shape; it is tall, slim and long-winged.
Do not paint gold-spangled upperparts or black underparts — that is Pacific Golden Plover.
Do not paint a broad white wing-bar in flight.
